province noun

also provinces, provincial

classical

M-O s.v. political division: province (Canada)

prōvincia, prōvinciae f.

noun, first declension

a province

Classically a territory outside Italy under a Roman governor, Sicily the first of them (Cic. Verr. 2.2.2); also any charge given to a magistrate, and in comedy any job one takes on (Plaut., Ter.). A modern province is a division of a country; Levi and Bini (p. 52) say to give prōvincia that new sense, or to use regiō.

Examples

  • prīma omnium, id quod ōrnāmentum imperī est, prōvincia est appellāta

    (Sicily) was the first of all to be called a province, the jewel of our empireCic. Verr. 2.2.2

  • Baetica … cūnctās prōvinciārum dīvitī cultū et quōdam fertilī ac peculiārī nitōre praecēdit

    Baetica outdoes all the provinces in the richness of its farming and a fertile brilliance of its ownPlin. NH 3.7

See also state, capital, empire.
